title: Best AI study apps for med students
summary: For medical school, use source-based review when you are learning a mechanism and card practice when you need to retrieve its parts.
body_markdown:
For medical school, use source-based review when you are learning a mechanism and card practice when you need to retrieve its parts. NotebookLM and Knowt serve those jobs differently. A polished summary alone gives little indication of whether you can reconstruct a mechanism.


Educato publishes this page and makes one of the apps on it. We list it where it fits, with its limits.

## Which study app is best for medical students using their own lecture notes?


Choose NotebookLM when you need to question a course source and Knowt when you already have material worth retrieving at intervals. Cover the arrows on a pathway diagram from class. Starting at the first box, draw the next link from memory and label what changes. Then ask what the model predicts if that link is interrupted. Compare your prediction with the lecture before keeping the question. If your notes leave the direction ambiguous, flag it for teaching staff instead of memorizing a generated explanation.


### Worked example: Reconstruct an oxygen dissociation graph


Imagine a physiology handout with two hemoglobin oxygen dissociation curves. The horizontal axis shows oxygen partial pressure and the vertical axis shows hemoglobin saturation. The second curve sits to the right of the first. The legend calls them A and B and gives no experimental conditions. Your assignment is to explain what the shift means using only the figure. Before asking an app to explain the graph, sketch both axes, label the curves and write down what you would hold constant to compare them.


A weak flashcard asks, “What does a right shift mean?” You might remember the phrase “lower affinity” and still put your pencil in the wrong place on the graph. Try a question you can grade with a ruler: “At a partial pressure in the steep part of the curves, which sample has the lower saturation? Show how you read it.” Draw a vertical line through that pressure. It meets B below A. A strong answer names B and explains that you compared heights at the same horizontal position.


Now run the comparison in reverse. Pick a saturation about halfway up the vertical axis and trace a horizontal line to each curve. Which sample needs the higher partial pressure to reach that saturation? The intersection with B falls farther to the right. If your answer says B has both lower saturation and higher pressure, ask which comparison you made. Each statement needs its own fixed quantity. A drawing with both guide lines makes that difference visible even if you forget the phrase you memorized.


There is a third question worth adding to this set: “Which experimental condition produced curve B?” The handout as described leaves that open. A plausible explanation from another lecture would still be a guess about this particular figure. A strong response identifies the missing evidence, such as a legend naming what changed between the samples. If the instructor later supplies a second figure with a labeled condition, save it separately. You now have one question about reading a relationship and another about explaining its cause.


At your next review, sketch the answer to the fixed-saturation question on blank paper before looking at either curve. Then open the handout and check the axis labels, the direction of your guide line and the order of the intersections. Record the specific error if you missed it. “Drew vertically when saturation was fixed” tells you exactly which card to revisit. “Review hemoglobin” sends you back through a whole lecture for a mistake you can correct on one drawing.


### NotebookLM


NotebookLM can assemble flashcards and audio overviews from your sources. Keep the anatomy lecture and its figure labels in the same notebook so you can check what the lecturer actually named. A source-grounded overview still deserves a check against the original diagram.[Read the product details](https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16213268?hl=en) .


Keep the handout and the corresponding lecture in one notebook. On mobile you can ask about the notebook sources or listen offline to a downloaded Audio Overview. For this figure, ask which source actually identifies A and B, then open its legend yourself. Audio can help you rehearse the verbal comparison while walking. Save the axis check for a moment when you can see the page and put your finger on an intersection.


NotebookLM is also called Gemini Notebook. The US prices in the table cover Google AI subscription bundles. Count the sources you intend to keep together for a block before paying for higher limits. A small physiology notebook containing a handout, the lecture and your corrections presents a different buying decision from a course archive that needs more than the personal account allowance in one notebook.


### Knowt


Knowt lets you create or import medical terminology cards and use free spaced repetition. Reserve the card deck for details you can check against a source. Ultra’s lecture summaries can help orient you to a recording before you return to its diagrams.[Read the product details](https://knowt.com/plans?tab=Student+Ultra) .


Once you can explain the drawing, make a short set whose prompts alternate between reading vertically and horizontally. Include a prompt that describes the axes without naming the topic. This catches a different mistake: recognizing a familiar picture quickly enough to recite the lecture caption before reading the question. Knowt Basic includes unlimited file creation, collaboration and storage. If a partner has already written accurate prompts, importing the cards for spaced practice gives you a concrete use for Knowt without buying lecture summaries.


### Educato


Best for a medical course whose examinable material is scattered across PDFs and annotated slides. Limits: full access is paid. A generated prompt can omit the qualifier that makes a lecture example work, so keep the source beside the answer.


Consider Educato when your lecturer distributes a clean slide but draws the comparison lines on the board. You can work from the presentation and a photo of your own annotated sketch. Ask Plumi to explain the question you missed, supplying the fixed quantity in your prompt. If speaking through a diagram is the feature you would pay for, try giving the explanation aloud with your paper sketch first. Listen for whether you name each axis and say what stays constant.


### Which task is worth paying for?


Look at the last physiology question you missed. If you misremembered what the lecturer assigned to curve B, spend your next session with the legend and the relevant source in NotebookLM. If you could explain both curves with the handout open but drew the guide line the wrong way the next morning, use Knowt’s retrieval practice. Student Ultra’s summaries and podcasts address another problem: getting through material presented in files and recordings. Decide whether that is where your study time actually goes before choosing a web subscription for the month or the year.
